subject: Pilot Pricing: Cache-first Packaging & Quant Guidance for Small-Scale Trial
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@avery-labs.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-27T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot inquiry - quant & cache guidance needed

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for taking the call this morning. Avery Labs is planning a small pilot (3-4 weeks) to validate LLM-powered summarization in our internal ops flows. Two asks from procurement & engineering: simple pilot pricing and guidance on whether we should focus on prefix/KV caching or aggressive quantization first.

Rough scale: ~150k prompt tokens total during pilot, low concurrency (single-digit qps), but strict 250ms latency target for short prompts.

Can you send recommended pilot structure (pricing, packaging) and any notes on expected quality tradeoffs for 4-bit vs int8 on open models? Also want a short SOW we can sign.

Appreciate it — Samir
Avery Labs — Procurement
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@avery-labs.com>
Date: 2025-06-27T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot inquiry - quant & cache guidance needed

Samir — thanks for the detail and for the clear latency requirement. Attached is a one-page SOW and a short technical spec (see attachments). High-level proposal and guidance below.

Pilot commercial proposal (recommended):
- Pilot fee: $18,000 flat (covers reserved capacity, support, and QA windows).
- Included credits: 120k token credits for generation/embedding during pilot.
- Post-pilot conversion: If Avery converts to committed capacity within 30 days, we apply a one-time 25% first-year discount on committed TPU/GPU usage pricing (tiered by commit band).
- Optional add-on: extended evaluation (extra 2 weeks) for $4,000.

Technical packaging guidance (cache-first recommendation):
- Cache-first approach (recommended for this profile): enable prefix/KV caching for repeated system/prompt prefixes and aggressive KV reuse for short-turn dialogs. For low concurrency and strict latency, caching reduces per-token compute and keeps p50/p90 latency consistent.
- Batching: keep small batch sizes (2-8) to avoid added latency spikes; continuous batching is fine if you cap max latency.
- Quantization path: start with int8 as default — good quality/throughput tradeoff. 4-bit (QLoRA-style) can reduce cost further but introduces nontrivial QA risk on summarization prompts; we recommend A/B testing 4-bit on a small held-out prompt set first and a rollback policy to int8 on quality regressions.

Quality guardrails we suggest including in SOW:
- Holdout eval set (10-20 prompts) to validate 4-bit vs int8 before production cutover; automated regression detection.
- Runtime fallback to int8 if eval slides below agreed threshold.

Next steps: review attached Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf and Quantization_Test_Spec.xlsx. If agreeable I can send an updated SOW with the 25% conversion discount and DocuSign link.

Attachments: Pilot_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf), Quantization_Test_Spec.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Pilot inquiry - cache-first suggestion + commercial ask (Avery Labs)

Looping you both in — Avery wants a 3-4 week pilot, low concurrency but tight latency, asked for pilot pricing and guidance on cache vs quantization. I proposed an $18k pilot + 120k token credits and a 25% first-year conversion discount.

Internal asks:
1) Can we sign off on the $18k pilot fee and the 25% conversion discount (recommendation: we can cap to a 12-month commitment and pre-defined commit bands)?
2) Monica: any quick notes on the QA delta between int8 and 4-bit for summarization? Should we require an eval window before offering 4-bit as a supported variant?

I attached the SOW and the quant test spec. Samir is asking for the DocuSign link once we confirm.

Thanks — Naomi
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-29T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot inquiry - cache-first suggestion + commercial ask (Avery Labs)

Naomi — quick technical read:
- Int8 path: solid + predictable. For summarization it keeps most of the semantic fidelity with ~12-20% throughput improvement vs fp16 depending on kernels. Recommended as the default.
- 4-bit path: can give another 30-40% token-cost reduction in ideal cases, but for extractive/abstractive summarization you often see hallucination risk and shorter context stability issues. Must be gated behind an eval.

Suggested guardrails to include in the pilot SOW:
- A/B evaluation over a 500-example holdout (we can run locally) with automated regression check (we pass if ROUGE/precision delta within agreed margins).
- Fallback policy: if 4-bit fails threshold during pilot, automatic fallback to int8 for the remainder; no extra charge for re-runs under the fallback.
- Pilot cap: cap billable token usage to 150k tokens to avoid runaway.

Commercial tradeoffs: if we require that gating and fallback, recommend final conversion discount be 25% (not 30) off list for year-one commit. We can offer 30% only for larger commit bands (>$250k annual). For small pilots, propose we accept 25% conversion discount and provide an extra 10k token credit as a goodwill for the gating overhead.

Attaching Quantization_Test_Spec.xlsx with suggested prompt set and evaluation metrics.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
